title: Thinking: Concept Formation, Metacognition, Problem Solving
summary: Concept formation strategies, metacognitive knowledge and regulation, problem solving strategies, barriers to problem solving, analogical reasoning.
revision: Concept formation: successive scanning, conservative focusing, focus gambling. Metacognition: knowledge + regulation. Problem solving: means-end analysis, working backward, analogical reasoning. Barriers: functional fixedness, mental set.
traps: Functional fixedness = inability to see alternative uses for objects.
Mental set = tendency to approach problems in a familiar way.
confusions: Confusing metacognitive knowledge (knowing about cognition) with regulation (controlling cognition).
Confusing functional fixedness with mental set.

notes.t: Concept formation involves learning to categorize objects, events, or ideas based on shared attributes. Strategies include successive scanning, conservative focusing, and focus gambling.
Metacognition is thinking about thinking. It includes metacognitive knowledge (knowledge about cognition) and metacognitive regulation (controlling cognition).
Problem solving strategies include means-end analysis, working backward, analogical reasoning, and breaking problems into subgoals.
Barriers include functional fixedness, mental set, and confirmation bias, which prevent effective problem solving.
Analogical reasoning involves solving a problem by drawing parallels with a similar, previously solved problem (positive transfer).
UGC NET frequently asks about metacognition, problem solving strategies, and barriers such as functional fixedness.
